lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: The stranger in the broad purple hat had been watching me from the other side of the old well for long enough that pretending not to notice her had become ridiculous.
You keep looking at the road as if you expect it to offer you a better idea.

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: I looked back at her. "Do you have one?"
Possibly. How attached are you to being ordinary?
A familiar's bond. Not a pet. Not a servant. A partner tied into my magic strongly enough that either of us could feel when the other was in danger.

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: "And what do you get out of it?"
Help. Company. Someone capable of telling me when I am about to do something clever and catastrophically stupid.
Then perhaps we have something to discuss. A familiar's bond. Partnership, not ownership.

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: "You say that very quickly."
Because I have met witches.

choices.text: "Start with what you can make me do."

lines.text: Very little by default. I may ask for your help on journeys, or with the House, and no more than half your daylight hours unless safety requires otherwise.
You are not to be treated as a slave or a pet. You may leave the House. You may refuse guests. You get a private room, the library, and—if you want it—access to mine at night.

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: "And if I decide you're becoming dangerous?"
I owe you teaching, access to my library, and protection from harm by my action or inaction. You keep freedom over your own body and whatever shape it takes.

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: "Whatever shape it takes?"
The bond should increase the size of both our magic. I do not know exactly how it will express itself in you.
You must be capable of stopping me if power makes me reckless or manipulative. The contract requires it.
And, unpleasantly, the reverse. If you become power-hungry or dangerous, I may compel you to stop. Only for that purpose.

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: "So we put a knife in each other's hands and call that trust?"
No. We acknowledge that trust without safeguards is just optimism.
No lies between us. No second magical bond that conflicts with this one. Mutual awareness of where the other is.

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: "I can live with that."

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: "No lies sounds broader than no betrayal."
It is. You may refuse to answer. You may say something is private. But if you answer me, it must be true. The same rule binds me.

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: "Fine. That I can agree to."
Then the contract needs blood, consent, and the name that is yours.

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: The nib scratched across the parchment: Marabeth Vale. The name looked like somebody else's coat hanging from my shoulders.

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: "Don't call me that."
I wasn't planning to. What should I call you?

choices.text: "I don't know. Pick something I can veto."

lines.text: Fox.

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: I waited for the name to feel ridiculous. It didn't.

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: "Fox. For now."

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: "Fox. For now, I think."
Fox, then.

lines.speaker: Fox
lines.text: The mark under my collarbone burned cold: three small crescents nested together. Then the rest of me stopped agreeing on what shape it was supposed to be.

lines.speaker: Fox
lines.text: For one breath I was too small, all heartbeat and whiskers. Then I was on four red-furred paws. Then upright again, ears too high, balance wrong, a tail lashing behind me because apparently I had one now.
Fox?

lines.speaker: Fox
lines.text: "I think I'm all right. I think."
Sit down before you discover another animal by falling over as it.
